summary:
# NOTES: *Whatsoever a Man Soweth* (William Le Queux, 1906; first-person, narrator Wilfrid Hughes; single novel, no book divisions)

## Cast
- **Wilfrid Hughes**: narrator. Antiquary, poor (~£1000/yr), chambers Bolton Street, Eton/Oxford. Family seat Netherdene (Sussex, let to Oldham cotton-spinner). Ex-sweetheart of Sybil. Valet **Budd**.
- **Hon. Eva Sybil "Tibbie" Burnet**: 23, 3rd daughter of late Viscount Scarcliff. Reckless, smart set. Maid **Mason**. Car: 60 h.p. Mercedes. Sisters **Cynthia** (m. Lord Wydcombe) and **Violet** (Countess of Alderholt). Mother **Lady Scarcliff** (Grosvenor Street/Place). Brother **Jack** (Viscount Scarcliff, 25, "The Scrambler", Stock Exchange, Magdalen friend of Winsloe). Butler **Adams**; under-butler **Rainer**; maid **Simmons**; chauffeur **Webber**.
- **Eric Domville**: Wilfrid's friend, "African explorer", Etonian, ~35, dark, bronzed. Actually an impostor (see Ch31).
- **Ellice Winsloe**: 38, tall, Cornish tin-mine family money, Jack's friend, proposed to Sybil ~fortnight before; she said she'd accept. Gang member.
- **Ryhall Place**: Sussex Tudor house (built by Sir Henry Burnet). Long Gallery, Dame Grace's Room, blue room, red drawing-room. Nearby: **East Marden**, **Charlton Wood**, Whitewater, Bow Hill, Elsted, Waltham, Midhurst.
- **Police/locals**: **Booth** (village constable, wife **Mrs Booth**), **Dr Richards**, **John Harris** (keeper), Superintendent (Chichester, short, thick-set).
- **The dead man**: called "Charles" by Eric; later identified as **Arthur Rumbold**. Letters from Sybil address "Ralph" (Vickers).
- **John Parham**: wholesale jeweller, house **Keymer**, Sydenham Hill; wife (~26, brown hair), maid **Jane** (killed), cook, gardener **Lane**, housemaid **Emily**. Alias **Sidney Humphreys** (bald, fair, "Zambesi" surveyor). Alias "Nello" (real name Lionel).
- **Laking** ('Arry): gate-keeper, Crystal Palace, Palace Park Road; sister **Annie** (Keymer cook's brother-in-law link).
- **Miss O'Hara**: dark-eyed girl, green New Zealand bracelet with diamond, Mrs Parham's companion.
- **Police**: **Inspector Pickering** (Tottenham Court Road, brown beard, 21 yrs London), sergeants **Edwards**, **Marvin**, **PC Horton**, **Inspector Nicholls**.
- **Camberwell**: **Mrs Williams** (landlady, Neate Street, ex-parlour-maid, Devon), husband **Williams** ("old man", mineral-water foreman).
- **Ralph Vickers**: sleek, smooth-haired, ex-convict (3 yrs), blackmailer/spy, lodged Vincent Square with Rumbold.
- **Arthur Rumbold**: son of Canon Rumbold (Lincoln, Folkingham), Guy's medical student. Mother Mrs Rumbold (elderly, grey, Fort William/Dumfries).
- **Charles Denton** (Pendleton, Manchester, 16b Bolton Road); letter from "R.W." (Bear Hotel, Devizes).
- **Fred Kinghorne**: American, Harewolde Abbey (Marstons), target.
- **Admiral Hellard**: Sybil's uncle, Albert Gate, Second Sea-Lord.

## Ch1–2: Ryhall, Long Gallery, sunset
- Sybil refuses to marry Wilfrid; says she'll marry Ellice ("mater approves, he's well off"). Anxious look; "I wonder if I might take you at your word"; then "My secret! ... You would hate me!" bursts into tears.
- Dinner; Sybil avoids Winsloe. Hilda Tracey at table.
- 2 a.m., Dame Grace's Room: Eric tells Wilfrid he overheard, ~3 p.m. in Charlton Wood, Sybil with a shabby man "Charles"; he claimed to be her lover; Sybil said she was engaged to Winsloe; he threatened to reveal "the truth" unless she married him; Eric saw revolver in Sybil's hand; shot heard ~4 p.m. (by Eric's watch).
- Rainer: man found shot dead in Charlton Wood by Harris.

## Ch3–4: Body in wood
- Booth: body found by Harris's dog; Mrs Booth sent word; telephone to Midhurst.
- Wilfrid & Eric cross fields, creep to wood. They search body in dark: take inner papers, wallet, pen-knife, receipt for registered letter, **gold locket/medallion** on broken chain. Eric's jacket over body; matches struck. Re-buttoned.
- Eric sees a figure in bushes near turnip field. Dr Richards & Booth arrive by dog-cart.
- Superintendent: "shot from the front"; dead ~8–9 hrs; no revolver; tab cut from coat. Inquest set: Spread Eagle, Midhurst.
- Eric's joke: "we didn't shoot with revolvers."
- Upstairs (Wilfrid's room): locket holds ivory miniature of Sybil; engraved "From Sybil—August 14th". Blood-stained letter.

## Ch5: The letters (texts; key lines)
- Hethe Hall (Cumberland) note: "I do wish, Ralph, you would be more careful"; Braithwaite Station 5:30; "Do not write... Mason... very curious."
- Serle Street outside Lincoln's Inn, Mason's clothes.
- "S.Y. Regina" green paper, off Faroe Islands; Glasgow; "From me the world shall never know the truth."
- "Why did you speak to me on the stairs last night?"
- "Let us part and agree to forget it." Mason suspects.
- Hotel Ritz Paris: "E—knows the truth. Avoid him... J—in the Bois"; £50 enclosed.
- Blue foreign paper, Durham: "I should have... married Wilfrid Hughes"; morphia/brandy; "I only crave humbly at your feet."
- Ryhall note: "I have kept my mouth closed."
- Cipher sheet; visiting card **Mr John Parham, Keymer, Sydenham Hill, S.E.**; pawn tickets (silver/ruby ring, Geneva watch; Fulham Road; name "Green").
- Sybil knocks at Wilfrid's door.

## Ch6–7: Midnight confession, flight
- Blue room: Sybil, black tailor-made, blue velvet bow. Admits "terrible" secret; asks Wilfrid to pretend to be her husband in Camberwell; he's compositor on morning paper; she's a working man's wife. Kisses his hand.
- Wilfrid agrees ("saving my life"). Advises she take Mason to Bournemouth (not Camberwell).
- Eric hid in wardrobe. Eric: "I can't see how being married protects her."
- ~3 a.m.: Sybil, Mason escape by the window; Mercedes glides down avenue; Sybil: "Thanks so much, Mr Hughes. Good-bye."
- Eric: Winsloe likely in love with her.

## Ch8: Morning after
- Winsloe, Jack, Wydcombe, Wilfrid visit barn. Winsloe goes white, says "entire stranger", identifies victim internally. Jack: "Seen him before" (Winsloe deflects).
- Lady Scarcliff at lunch: note from Tibbie: "Perhaps I shall be back to-morrow."
- Wilfrid & Eric search Winsloe's kitbag: cheap carte-de-visite of dead man (dark tweed suit, golf cap).

## Ch9: Camberwell and Mason's dress
- Thursday night, King's Cross, 8 p.m. Sybil in Mason's black jacket and hat; wedding ring from Regent Street (Wilfrid's).
- Cover story: Mrs Morton née lady's-maid, married ~1 yr. Names: **William & Molly Morton** ("Willie"/"Molly").
- Hansom to Elephant & Castle. Sybil's route: Bournemouth Bath Hotel; night Birmingham (Grand), Bull Street, Leicester.
- Mason returns to Ryhall; Lady Scarcliff anxious.

## Ch10: Neate Street
- Budd suspicious of Wilfrid's cheap suit.
- Lodgings: Neate Street, Camberwell (Mrs Williams). Pretext: no kitchen at other places.
- Williams, mineral-water foreman; friendly, "beer and pipe".
- Eric back at Bolton Street; reports Winsloe went to Harker's Hotel (Waterloo Road) inquiring for Sybil.

## Ch11: Winsloe and a girl
- Eric saw Winsloe in Ryhall park with shabby young woman (violets on hat, fur tippet), he gave money.
- Winsloe recalled to London; Eric followed him.
- Sybil terrified, "Winsloe knows that I was there"; says she'll kill herself if found.
- Wilfrid advised to stay away; ignores.

## Ch12: Pawnbroker, Sydenham
- Pawnbroker: pledger had short brown beard, "Green"; ruby ring worth ~£80.
- Park Lane: Winsloe, "I'm strolling back to the Burlington."
- Sydenham Hill: Keymer. Lamplighter; Laking gives Parham gossip: "wrong 'un"; Parham beat by Mrs Parham's brother; wife attempted sublimate suicide.
- Wilfrid & Laking visit kitchen; Annie (cook) terrified: "There's a curse on this 'ouse."

## Ch13–14: The attack at Keymer
- Drawing-room: Mrs Parham chloroformed on blue sofa; maid **Jane** gagged with black striped scarf, unconscious then dead. Lane, Emily present.
- Wilfrid pockets the dead man's photograph from table (bigger cabinet portrait, red leather frame).
- Floor: carpet torn; cavity under board in corner, steel-lined; empty.
- Red morocco case with a preserved human eye (doctor takes it).
- Mrs Parham: husband away (Paris, Amsterdam). Inspector: "the lady is lying."

## Ch15: Three weeks
- Sybil works in Neate Street; sends groceries to poor.
- Eric: Parham "may go to India"; Wilfrid to call on Mrs Parham.
- Sybil: "I fear lest I may be discovered by those enemies." Wilfrid: "Ellice Winsloe... now intends to denounce you!" Sybil: "Who told you so?"

## Ch16: Boodle's and the stairs
- Winsloe invites Wilfrid to Boodle's; probes. Mentions "Humphreys" introduction later.
- Empire: Winsloe meets **Sidney Humphreys** (bald, fair, Zambesi; invites to see antiques, "second floor" rooms off a dark street east of Regent Street).
- Wilfrid hears Eric's voice: "I defy you!" Groan, shriek. Four stairs give way; Wilfrid falls; skull hit.

## Ch17: Sewer
- Wilfrid wakes in London main sewer, thigh-deep, rats. Poland Street plaque. Flush (automatic) threat. Shaft/ladder; grating at Oxford Street, corner Hart Street, Bloomsbury.
- Newsboy fetches constable; sewerman; Inspector Pickering takes card. Sewerman says body of woman in sewer near Charing Cross Road; man in evening dress at Beckton outfall.

## Ch18: Cipher and the paper
- Wilfrid's bruised head; Budd told to say Wilfrid absent.
- Decodes agony-column ad: "White Feather reports W.H. gone home. Nothing to fear."
- Sybil gives Wilfrid cipher ad for **Daily Telegraph**: "To Nello.—Will make appointment... Note that Eric is in Paris. I still trust you.—S." Wilfrid decodes.

## Ch19: Leeds
- Leeds lodging (Roundhay Road); Temple Newsham walk. Sybil: "Before evil fell upon me."
- Telegraph reply: "To S.—You have been betrayed! Exercise caution..."
- Wilfrid sends Sybil to Newcastle (Douglas Hotel, Grainger Street West); Wilfrid's own cipher ad to Nello: "Meet me outside Baker Street Station to-night at eight."
- Wilfrid takes Caledonian Hotel, Adelphi Terrace; Budd is his agent.
- Winsloe seen at Burlington; General Taylor (Albany).

## Ch20: Baker Street
- Dark-eyed girl (O'Hara) at Baker Street; Wilfrid follows her by train (Lordship Lane), up Sydenham Hill to Keymer.
- Mrs Parham & O'Hara; Wilfrid's name given as "William Morton".
- Pickering: plain-clothes saw Wilfrid with Parham and another man at Empire; Winsloe's accomplice = Humphreys (= Parham).

## Ch21: Dean's Yard
- Cipher ad "To White Feather.—... Dean's Yard, Westminster, at nine... S."
- 10 p.m. trio: Parham (evening clothes), thin-faced accomplice, costermonger (pearl buttons) signal whistle; cab waiting; O'Hara arrives; they scatter. Plot assumed to target Sybil.

## Ch22: Manchester and the letter
- Receipt: registered letter from Blandford (Dorset) addressed "Charles Denton, 16b Bolton Road, Pendleton".
- Wilfrid, as "Harry Williams", steals registered letter from Denton's landlady (Mrs Denton's lodger, away 4 months).
- Letter from **R.W.**, Bear Hotel, Devizes: "Sybil fears me, and will pay... Meet me in Chichester at the Dolphin next Sunday... Ellice has already touched a good deal of the Scarcliffs' money from young Jack."
- Postscript: "Ellice believes that Sybil still loves Wilfrid Hughes. This is incorrect... She loves **Arthur Rumbold**."

## Ch23: Trail north
- Carlisle: Sybil recognised by friend; note she went to Glasgow then Dumfries (misdirection); actually to Fort William.
- Glasgow Central Station: hall-porter; bald-headed man (Parham) visited.
- Fort William: Mrs Morton (maid) with **Mrs Rumbold**.
- Oban (Alexandra hotel). Back to Glasgow, then Dumfries Railway Hotel. Sybil "alone" in room.
- Mrs Rumbold interview: Wilfrid says "Sybil... love for Arthur"; she is shocked: "Arthur—my boy."

## Ch24–25: Newcastle, Leazes Park
- Sybil in Douglas Hotel. Sybil in Leazes Park; wants to die; "I must die!"; "vanquished".
- Her "love" for Arthur Rumbold; married? "Is it folly to love a man whom one can never marry?"
- Sybil tells Wilfrid of Parham's threat; "Nello". Blackmail generalised.
- Parham seen in Newcastle, approaching Douglas Hotel; Sybil escapes in closed cab; back to London.

## Ch26: Watch
- Neate Street: Mrs Williams: two foreign men inquired about Wilfrid & "Mrs Morton" (French agents). Wilfrid says "in Ireland".
- Wilfrid watches Winsloe: Curzon Street (Wydcombes), Grosvenor Place, Scarcliffs. Winsloe takes a parcel from Keymer to Winsloe's King Street chambers; Parham meets him at Trocadero.
- Parham follows to **Clipstone Street** (between Cleveland St and Great Portland St): unoccupied house with iron ink-man extinguishers. Parham lives Lyric Chambers, Whitcomb Street.
- Wilfrid to Pickering at Tottenham Court Road police station.

## Ch27: House of Doom
- Pickering, Edwards, Marvin; Edwards picks front door latch. Dining rooms; study.
- Stairs: first six from top hinge; trap pit. Settle as bridge.
- Pale-green room: Eric's room (defiance); **Wilfrid's silver cigarette-case** given to Eric (2 yrs ago) found on mantel.
- Drawer: emerald necklace, pearls; **Eric's amethyst signet ring**.
- Bare bedroom: **blood stain** on carpet; broken chair; torn lace curtain.
- Prisoner's room: barred window, sheet-iron door, bread crust.
- Parcel from Winsloe: French securities (~£20,000).

## Ch28: Well and Sybil's letter
- Rope-ladder down a well shaft; spring; culverts to main sewer; iron bar with bit of blue brocade and chiffon (death trap).
- Letter from Harewolde Abbey (Herefordshire), in Sybil's hand, about **Fred Kinghorne** (American, Wall Street father, Cecil Hotel, Naples).
- Front door: key clicks. Man enters. Pickering: "I arrest you on suspicion..." — it is **Eric Domville** (not Parham), white, guilty-looking.

## Ch29: Eric arrested; Vickers
- Eric: "The police are fools." Taken to station (Edwards, Marvin).
- Night watch; second man enters at dawn: **Ralph Vickers** (dark-haired, travelling coat), German bank-notes, just back from Germany. "That woman has betrayed us—Sybil Burnet... she shall pay."
- Pickering: Sybil must be questioned. Wilfrid promises she'll answer.

## Ch30: Sybil's confession
- Sybil reveals (to Wilfrid at Neate Street) Vickers's first meeting: train Gare du Nord–Calais; schoolgirl at Madame Perrin's, Versailles; Allée des Sabotiers.
- Took box "Bohemian liqueur glasses" to uncle **Admiral Hellard** (Albert Gate). Box contained French submarine plans from a naval lieutenant; British Admiralty paid Vickers £3000.
- Vickers blackmails: French extradition threat (Sybil born at father's villa, Cannes).
- Sybil meets **Arthur Rumbold** after tyre-burst near Stretton (Great North Road); Rumbold had rooms in Vincent Square with Vickers.
- Rumbold learns of Clipstone Street house; Charlton Wood meeting: man (Eric, using name "Charles") shot Rumbold dead.

## Ch31: Conclusion
- Sybil: Eric = impostor, Vickers's agent; real Eric Domville lives in Cape Town; Eric also "Charles Denton" in Manchester. "Nello" = Parham (Lionel).
- Wilfrid: his own false deduction; Eric (cell) swallowed strychnine pill.
- Sybil: marriage made her British, beyond French law (why she asked Wilfrid to pose).
- Police: Parham arrested at Clipstone Street; Vickers and Parham await trial (blackmail, robbery, murder); Winsloe fled to Buenos Aires (not arrested). Mrs Parham learns husband wanted in France (Bordeaux banker murder). Miss O'Hara explained cipher behind wardrobe.
- Family assembly: Jack, Cynthia, Wydcombe, Lady Scarcliff. Wilfrid proposes "real" marriage; Jack: "You've saved her, and you've a right to her."
- Ending: Wilfrid & Sybil live near **Amersham, Buckinghamshire** (home given by Lady Scarcliff as wedding present).
- Motto: "*Whatsoever a Man Soweth, that shall he also Reap.*" The End.
